Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ensure verb

see to it that something happens

also see to it, see that, take care that, make certain that

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.20.3: cūrā ut valeās
Plaut. Am. 1.2.25; Cic. Div. 1.48 (Lewis & Short)

cūrō, cūrāre, cūrāvī, cūrātum

verb, first conjugation: ut or nē and the subjunctive

see to it (that), take care (that)

The everyday way, in speech and in letters: cūrā ut valeās, “see that you keep well”, is how Cicero ends a letter. Its first sense is “look after, take care of” (cūrāre corpus), and with an accusative and a gerundive it is “have something done” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — see (to it) that

    verb, second conjugation: in this sense with ut or nē and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.1.2: nāvem idōneam ut habeās, dīligenter vidēbis (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly as a request or an order: vidē ut, vidēbis ut, videndum est ut. Vidē nē is also a warning, “mind you don’t …”, and vidē quid agās “think what you are doing”.

  • efficiō, efficere, effēcī, effectum — bring it about that

    verb, third conjugation (-iō): ut and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 59 (Lewis & Short)

    When the result takes work or contrivance; its general sense is “cause, bring about” (see cause).

Examples

  • nāvem idōneam ut habeās, dīligenter vidēbis

    you will take good care to have a suitable shipCic. Fam. 16.1.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • ventus incrēbrēscit. cūrā ut valeās.

    the wind’s getting up. Take care of yourself.Cic. Fam. 7.20.3

  • Cūrā ut jānua clausa sit.

    Make sure the door is shut.composed

  • Cūrā (cūrāte) ut …

    See to it that …Traupman 376

See also sure, cause, achieve.
